q: A hair dryer converts _____ . (2024)
e: A hair dryer converts electrical energy into thermal energy to produce heat.

q: The _____ the bond enthalpy, the more energy needed to break the bond, and the stronger is the bond. (2025)
e: The higher the bond enthalpy, the more energy is needed to break the bond, and the stronger the bond is. A lower, smaller, or unchanged value would not make the bond stronger.

q: Standard enthalpy change of formation is _____ for endothermic reaction. (2026)
e: An endothermic change takes heat in, so the standard enthalpy change of formation is positive. It is negative only when the formation gives heat out, and zero only for an element in its standard state.

q: Combustion of fuels in a/an _____ process. (2025)
e: Burning a fuel releases heat, so combustion of fuels is an exothermic process. Heat absorbing describes an endothermic change, the opposite of combustion.

q: The symbol for bond enthalpy is _____. (2024)
e: In this Grade 12 course the symbol for bond enthalpy is E, as in E(C-H). ΔH_f is enthalpy of formation and ΔH_r is enthalpy of reaction. ΔH_b is not the symbol the chapter uses.

q: The standard enthalpy change of _____ is the enthalpy change when solutions of an acid and an alkali react together under standard conditions to produce one mole of water. (2025)
e: Neutralisation is the enthalpy change when an acid and alkali react under standard conditions to produce one mole of water.

q: Change in enthalpy of a system is due to the heat supplied at a constant _____. (2025)
e: Enthalpy change is the heat supplied to a system at constant pressure. Mass is not the condition that defines an enthalpy change.

q: The highly accurate values of the standard enthalpy change of combustion (ΔH°_c) can be measured only by a _____. (2026)
e: A bomb calorimeter is used for accurate measurements of standard enthalpy changes of combustion.

q: Specific heat capacity of liquid is the energy required to raise the temperature of _____ of liquid by 1°C. (2025)
e: Specific heat capacity is defined as the heat required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of liquid by 1°C.

q: Automobile engines can change _____ into mechanical energy. (2025)
e: An automobile engine burns fuel, so it changes chemical energy into mechanical energy. Changing chemical energy into electrical energy is what a battery does.

q: The symbol for bond enthalpy is _____. (2025)
e: In this Grade 12 course the symbol for bond enthalpy is E. ΔH_b is not the symbol used here. ΔH_r is a reaction enthalpy and ΔH_sol is the enthalpy of solution.

q: The energy needed to make or break bonds is called _____. (2025)
e: The energy needed to make or break bonds is bond enthalpy, also called bond energy. A bond angle is the angle between two bonds, not an energy.

q: When ice melts at room temperature is a _____ process. (2025)
e: Ice melting at room temperature is a spontaneous, endothermic process.

q: The numerical value of specific heat capacity of water is _____. (2024)
e: The specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 J g^-1 °C^-1. 4.81 J g^-1 °C^-1 is not that value, and 4.18 g J^-1 has the units reversed.

q: Which one of the following energy transformations takes place in solar cell? (2025)
e: A solar cell changes light energy into electrical energy. Chemical energy into electrical energy is the change in a battery, not in a solar cell.

q: Standard enthalpy change is measured at _____ and 760 mmHg. (2025)
e: Standard enthalpy change is measured at 25°C and 760 mmHg. 0°C and 273 K are the same gas-law temperature, not the thermochemical standard. 25°C is 298 K, not 295 K.

q: The specific heat capacity of water is _____. (2025)
e: The specific heat capacity of water is 4.18 J g^-1 °C^-1. 4.18 kJ g^-1 °C^-1 is a thousand times too large, and 4.81 J g^-3 °C^-1 uses the wrong number and the wrong mass unit.

q: E (C-H) refers to the bond enthalpy of a _____ of single bonds between carbon and hydrogen atoms. (2025)
e: Bond enthalpy refers to the energy required per mole of single bonds.

q: The symbol of standard enthalpy changes for HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) is expressed as _____. (2025)
e: The reaction between acid and base is neutralisation, represented by ΔH°_n.

q: The highly accurate values of the standard enthalpy change of _____ can be measured. (2026)
e: The highly accurate standard enthalpy change measured with a bomb calorimeter is the enthalpy change of combustion. Neutralisation is measured in a solution calorimeter, not a bomb.

q: The enthalpy change of _____, of a substance is the heat change that occurs when one mole of a substance is dissolved in water. (2026)
e: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance dissolves in water is the enthalpy change of solution. Neutralisation is an acid reacting with an alkali to make one mole of water.
